title: GPUParticles2D blocks the main thread for a long time when instantiated
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: 4.5.1, 4.6-rc ### System information Godot v4.6.rc.mono (481f36ed2) - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6070) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10750H CPU @ 2.60GHz (12 threads) - 63.86 GiB memory ### Issue description When GPUParticles2D are spawned and enter view, there is a large stutter as the pipeline for the `ParticleProcessMaterial` gets compiled. In our project, since we wish to avoid these stutters, we are attempting to do the "dumb" thing of showing all particles at once behind a black screen. This causes the game to become unresponsive for about a minute and a half. I believe this PR was a step towards solving this issue: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/90400 But after thoroughly inspecting the code and doing lots of profiling, I believe that it either never worked for GPU particles or there was a regression related to the `ParticleProcessMaterial` sometime afterwards. To go deeper into what we're seeing: - In `ParticlesStorage.set_code`, `version_set_compute_code` calls `_shader_rd._compile_version_start`, which begins a compilation in the background. But then, right afterward, the call to `version_is_valid` in `ERR_FAIL_COND` forces the main thread to wait on the compilation. - Even if this is removed, the call to `ParticlesShaderRD.version_get_shader` further down _also_ causes the main thread to wait. - And if this is placed in a background thread (e.g. if it is made part of the worker thread task within `PipelineDeferredRD.create_compute_pipeline`), then a call further up the chain to `MaterialStorage.material_set_shader` causes a material update (`ParticleProcessMaterialData.update_parameters`) to be `CallQueue`'d to the main thread, which results once again in `ParticlesShaderRD.version_get_shader` blocking the main thread. This is where I reached my limits of how far I could understand the rendering stack. ### Steps to reproduce - Clear all shader caches (NVidia shader cache, `shader_cache` in `user://`, `shader_cache` in `.godot`) - Create several different `GPUParticles2D` with different permutations of options (e.g. turbulence on/off, different emission shapes) - Place them all into a scene - Run the scene - Observe that the scene takes a long time to show up ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [gpu-particles-slow.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24623356/gpu-particles-slow.zip) This MRP contains over 500 particle process materials. They are all saved directly from our main project. The GPUParticles2D themselves are default instances created only to house the particle process materials. If you run it, you will see that it takes over a minute to reach the scene. Profiling the application results in this pattern of calls, repeated over a minute.
